claims.text: Adding a small amount of Ti to Co-free FeNiCrMn will improve its dynamic mechanical performance.
The proposed intervention is the addition of a small amount of Ti.
Ti addition will form Ti-rich precipitates in FeNiCrMn.
Ti addition will produce solid-solution strengthening in FeNiCrMn.
Precipitation hardening from Ti will enhance the alloy's strength and ductility.
Solid-solution strengthening from Ti will enhance the alloy's strength and ductility.
Ti-modified FeNiCrMn will have greater strength under dynamic loading than unmodified FeNiCrMn.
Ti-modified FeNiCrMn will have greater ductility under dynamic loading than unmodified FeNiCrMn.
The claimed improvement applies from -200°C to 500°C.
The claimed improvement applies from strain rates of 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The optimal amount of Ti is uncertain.
The microstructural changes resulting from Ti addition are uncertain.
Ti-modified and unmodified FeNiCrMn will be compared using split-Hopkinson pressure-bar testing.
Stress-strain curves and fracture toughness will be measured.
The hypothesis is falsified if Ti-modified FeNiCrMn shows no significant improvement in strength and ductility relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis covers strain rates down to 10^-3 s^-1, but split-Hopkinson pressure-bar testing alone ordinarily addresses high-rate loading and therefore does not operationally test the full stated strain-rate range.
